title: Is your favorite fitness channel tra$h?
summary: NH lists six red flags for fitness YouTube channels: no discussion of programming, focus on a gimmick, promises of quick results, PED use, obsession with diet, and constant product selling. One flag can be tolerated, two call for caution, and three mean you should unsubscribe.
claims: TikTok and Instagram are far worse than YouTube for fitness advice and should be avoided entirely
Rate a channel by red flags: one is a flaw, two means be wary, three means unsubscribe
Programming is everything for naturals past the novice stage; a channel that never discusses volume, intensity or frequency ignores what drives progression
Channels built around one gimmick, especially endless exercise-selection videos, feed beginners' attention spans without making them bigger
A creator who turns into a caricature of himself has stopped being informative and become a circus
Promises of results in days or weeks are a red flag; building muscle is slow and quick fixes leave you looking the same a year later
Enhanced creators are disconnected from natural reality, so their advice doesn't fit natural viewers
Fitness YouTubers profit from viewers who never progress, because progress would mean you stop needing them
About 90% of a natural lifter's fitness subscriptions should be natural creators
Training is the main driver of physique and eating is the easy part; diet-obsessed channels cater to people who avoid training
Channels that constantly sell products are infomercials aimed at your wallet, and these sellers often also obsess over diet and are enhanced
These six criteria rule out about 95% of fitness YouTubers, roughly nine out of ten
